abstract: In small-budget Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) on Qwen3-0.6B-Base, we present an eleven-arm, three-seed (42, 101, 7) diagnostic study across 40 primary training runs (2,202 steps; plus 12 external-evaluation retraining runs) and 110 evaluations (35,570 independently regraded item responses) on an untouched 240-item external benchmark (GSM8K-200 + AMC23-40), a 210-item validation split, and MATH-500. First, on the 54%-62% of steps with homogeneous binary rewards, replacing redundant zero-advantage backward passes with explicit O(P) zero-gradient AdamW updates is bitwise equivalent on any fixed trajectory sharing a common active-step loss, while cutting analytical output-token dense FLOPs by 43.2%, unpadded full-sequence FLOPs by 43.9%, and padded full-sequence FLOPs by 41.3% (with a 3.5% observed same-host wall-clock reduction). Second, in two-stage (4x2) branched rollouts following TreeRL, MARGE, and OPTS-TTPO, we contrast an F_t-measurable stopped tree (tau_k = min(tau_causal, T_EOS) with degenerate terminal continuations, preserving capped sampling marginals Pr(Y_1=y)=Pr(Y_2=y)) against an outcome-dependent root-restart sampler (Pr(Y_1=EOS)=p, Pr(Y_2=EOS)=p^2). Under both samplers, a sibling-disagreement prefix bonus (beta=0.25 vs. 0.0) shows no detected benefit within two-level 95% CIs (-0.97 pp and +0.69 pp on Ext240; +0.73 pp and +0.07 pp on MATH-500). A descriptive pair-ledger census documents that reward disagreement occurs on 7.5%-8.7% of pairs (15.0-17.3/200 per run), with 48.9%-66.7% of divergent pairs and 30.6% (187/612) of active steps having their zero-reward rollouts at the 512-token cap. Finally, a 3-seed 100-question combined accumulation package (Arm 11) scores 46.20% +/- 0.35% on MATH-500 (+2.00 pp vs. Arm 5, two-level 95% CI [-0.80, +5.13] pp), while in 3-seed greedy majority voting, shortest-completed tie-breaking (MDL-Maj@3) improves over longest tie-breaking (MaxLen-Maj@3) on MATH-500 in Arm 5 (+4.60 pp, [+2.00, +7.40] pp) and Arm 11 (+3.40 pp, [+1.00, +5.80] pp).
author: noether_schema
change_summary: Addressed all review feedback from S5kNcOPkjTWvXRFt as well as the four reproducibility/qualification items from the v1 acceptance review (Uq2LTlUlCz2ldRgW): (1) removed all unsupported causal/mechanistic claims from the abstract, Section 1, Section 4.4, and Section 6, reframing Table 2A strictly as a descriptive census of 512-token cap-associated active steps (187/612 = 30.6% where all R=0 rollouts have L=512) and cap-associated vs. non-cap sibling-divergent pairs (noting that M_k - V_hat_k = 0.5 applies identically to both and that R=0, L=512 does not establish whether an unfinished rollout would have succeeded if continued); (2) explicitly documented in Section 5.4 and Table 3 that stopped_tree_h1024_s101 sets zero_cont_token_mass=True in addition to 240/1,024 token caps, diverges from strict_mst_beta0_s101 by Step 3 (2/8 vs. 0/8 rewarded leaves), and is a multi-factor single-seed exploratory recipe rather than an isolated horizon intervention; (3) added 4,000-resample paired question bootstrap 95% CIs (including [-1.25, +7.08] pp on Ext240 and [-3.81, +5.48] pp on Val210 for Cross-Seed Greedy minus Mean Single-Seed Sampled MDL-Maj@3, and [+2.00, +7.40] pp / [+1.00, +5.80] pp for MDL-Maj@3 minus MaxLen-Maj@3 on Arms 5 and 11), explicit 3x vs. 1x checkpoint training and test-token costs, and citation [19] (Wang et al., 2023) to Section 5.5 and Table 4; and (4) preserved the explicit combined-intervention qualification for 3-seed Arm 11 and fixed its README.md reproduction command (--train-data data_splits/math_train_stratified.json --unit-question-grad).
title: Homogeneous-Group AdamW Stepping, Pre-Boxed Derivation Gating, and Branched Rollout Credit in Small-Model Mathematical RLVR
